stories.title: Mali: Damning Evidence of War Crimes By State Armed Forces and Wagner Group Personnel - New Report
stories.summary: Mali: Damning Evidence of War Crimes By State Armed Forces and Wagner Group Personnel - New Report U.S. Ken Bergmann/Wikimedia Commons Members of the Malian army conduct drills (file photo). 29 September 2026 Amnesty International (London) Killings of civilians during military joint operations Civilians tortured to death in detention, others subjected to simulated drowning, beatings and electric shocks Fulani, Arabs and Tuaregs targeted Members of Mali's armed forces working together with personnel from the Wagner Group committed war crimes, including the murder and torture of civilians, during joint operations between 2023 and 2025, Amnesty International said in a new report. 'No one is spared': War crimes committed by the Malian army and foreign allied forces along the Mauritanian border documents the killings of at least 34 civilians in seven localities in Mali between June 2023 and December 2025, committed by the Malian armed forces (Forces armées maliennes - FAMa) and the Wagner Group (a Russian private military company active in Mali between late 2021 and June 2025). Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn READ OUR REPORT: 'No one is spared': War crimes committed by the Malian army and foreign allied forces along the Mauritanian border The report also documents other serious violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law, such as torture, enforced disappearance, and the pillaging and destruction of civilian property. "Our conclusions paint a harrowing picture of the lives of civilians trapped in the conflict, paying the ultimate price while impunity remains rampant. The Malian authorities cannot dismiss these serious allegations without opening impartial and effective investigations into the alleged crimes," said Marceau Sivieude, Amnesty International's Regional Director for West and Central Africa. "They must protect civilians during military operations, comply with and ensure respect for international humanitarian law, urgently clarify the chain of command under which foreign personnel act in the country, and monitor their conduct through an independent, domestic accountability mechanism." Unlawful killings of civilians The report provides details of seven incidents during which 34 people were unlawfully killed in the Ségou, Mopti and Timbuktu regions. Based on information gathered by Amnesty International, none of the victims were taking direct part in hostilities at the time of their deaths.

stories.title: États-Unis – Érythrée : pourquoi Washington tourne la page des sanctions contre Asmara

stories.title: Journalist to be crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute
stories.summary: Image source, Ngabo Amon/BBC By Basillioh Rukanga Â and Â Bella Twine ,Â BBC Focus on Africa Published 29 September 2026, 00:44 BST Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma Nyabongo I, who is set to be crowned king of Uganda's Tooro kingdom later, has long been a familiar face in the country. For many Ugandans, he was known not as the heir to the throne, but as a storyteller, as a long-serving anchor and editor at the state broadcaster. But Kijanangoma, 56, has now become the subject of media attention himself - his rise to the Tooro throne sparking controversy and widespread reactions beyond the country. Tooro is one of Uganda's four main officially recognised historical kingdoms. For the last 31 years, it has been headed by King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who was once known as a "boy king", after ascending to the throne as an infant.

stories.title: En Algérie, qui sont les fidèles parmi les fidèles d’Abdelmadjid Tebboune ?
stories.summary: Réélu en septembre 2024, le président algérien s’appuie sur un noyau dur de fidèles forgé dans l’épreuve. Voici les hommes de l’ombre au cœur du palais d’El Mouradia.

stories.title: Dette du Sénégal : pourquoi l’accord avec le FMI comporte encore des zones d’ombre
stories.summary: Le Sénégal n’a pas encore reçu un dollar du FMI, mais l’accord du 1er septembre a déjà fait bouger les marchés. L’économiste Florent Kanga Gbongué analyse les vraies marges de manœuvre du pays dans les colonnes de The Conversation.

stories.title: Au Maroc, un an après le mouvement de la « gen Z », des centaines de détenus et une chape de plomb
stories.summary: Au total, près de 5 700 personnes ont été arrêtées pendant et après les manifestations de la jeunesse entre septembre et octobre 2025, dont 650 sont toujours en prison. stories.title: ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys
stories.summary: The baboons’ presence has affected house prices on the Cape Peninsula, as they raid bins and kitchens and poo on properties. The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered.

stories.title: Sadio Mané, la star du football, se lance dans la transformation des mangues au Sénégal
stories.summary: L’ancien attaquant de Liverpool a posé, le 19 septembre, la première pierre d’une usine qui produira de la pulpe de mangue, de la mangue séchée, mais aussi du beurre de mangue, dans son village natal, en Casamance.

stories.title: Fusillades en Afrique du Sud : au moins 27 morts dans deux bars au Cap et à Johannesburg
stories.summary: A Johannesburg, huit assaillants armés de fusils d’assaut ont abattu 17 clients, tandis que 10 personnes ont été tuées dans un township proche du Cap. Les motifs de ces attaques restent inconnus selon la police.

stories.title: I have seen with pride how British overseas aid saves children’s lives. That is why I say cuts should be reversed | David Harewood
stories.summary: ‘UK funding for Sierra Leone’s newborn care programme is now expected to end in December 2026, two years earlier than planned.’ Photograph: Jonathan Porter/Alamy View image in fullscreen ‘UK funding for Sierra Leone’s newborn care programme is now expected to end in December 2026, two years earlier than planned.’ Photograph: Jonathan Porter/Alamy I have seen with pride how British overseas aid saves children’s lives. That is why I say cuts should be reversed David Harewood I understand the pressure on the public purse, but I have also seen the effect of our spending on the ground. Before those discussions begin, I want ministers to picture a hospital ward I visited in Sierra Leone with Unicef (United Nations Children’s Fund). Inside the special-care baby unit at Makeni regional hospital were rows of tiny premature babies, some no bigger than my hand.

stories.summary: Une partie de cette somme, 380 millions d’euros, sera allouée en Afrique subsaharienne pour le financement d’actions liées aux migrations, « axées sur la protection des migrants vulnérables, le soutien au retour volontaire et à la réintégration », selon un communiqué.

stories.title: JOJ de Dakar 2026 : le Sénégal dans les starting-blocks
stories.summary: JOJ de Dakar 2026 : le Sénégal dans les starting-blocks Sécurité, logistique, transports, hébergement… À quelques semaines du coup d’envoi des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (31 octobre-13 novembre) – la première compétition olympique organisée sur le sol africain –, la capitale sénégalaise, ville hôte, est dans la dernière ligne droite des préparatifs. stories.title: Ensemencer les nuages pour les faire pleuvoir : solution miracle ou mirage ?
stories.summary: Faire pleuvoir les nuages, ce n’est pas de la science-fiction. Utilisée en Afrique depuis plusieurs décennies, cette technique ne s’y est pourtant jamais vraiment imposée. Mais la multiplication des sécheresses pourrait la remettre au goût du jour.

stories.title: Comment le Rassemblement national tente de se constituer des réseaux dans le monde arabe
stories.summary: Convaincus d’arriver au pouvoir en 2027, Marine Le Pen et Jordan Bardella, conscients qu’il leur faudrait alors dialoguer avec tous les pays, cherchent des interlocuteurs au Maghreb et au Moyen-Orient. stories.title: Côte d’Ivoire : ces femmes qui font l’économie
stories.summary: Pétrole, mines, télécoms… De plus en plus de femmes sont aux manettes dans des secteurs économiques de premier plan en Côte d’Ivoire. Avec la performance, l’innovation et l’ambition comme mots d’ordre.

stories.summary: Premier ministre sous Lansana Conté, devenu opposant à Alpha Condé puis à Mamadi Doumbouya, Sidya Touré est mort ce vendredi 25 septembre à Paris, à l’âge de 81 ans. En exil en Côte d’Ivoire depuis 2022, il souhaitait finir ses jours en Guinée.

stories.title: Législatives au Maroc : « Le vote du monde rural est toujours déterminant »

stories.title: Are Ethiopians marching back to war in Tigray?
stories.summary: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Tigrayan forces have been patrolling the streets of Tigray's capital, Mekelle, this week By Lucy Fleming Â and Â BBC Africa Published 26 September 2026 Fighting has erupted in Ethiopia's northern region of Tigray between regional forces and the national army. Tigray residents, who have been trying to recover from a brutal two-year war that ended in 2022, fear a return to full-scale conflict. There are reports of panic buying - and now internet and call services have been disrupted. This means people cannot get access to their money via digital apps in what has become a largely cashless society after ATMs stopped working several months ago. Why has fighting broken out now?

stories.title: South African white genocide does not exist, new ambassador to US tells BBC
stories.summary: Figure caption, Are claims of a white genocide in South Africa real? By Ione Wells ,Â in Washington ,Â Mayeni Jones ,Â in Johannesburg Â and Â Ed Habershon ,Â in Johannesburg Published 26 September 2026 South Africa's new ambassador to Washington has a personal reason to challenge Donald Trump's assertion that there is a genocide against white Afrikaners - he is "a born Afrikaner" himself. "Is he talking about us?" Roelf Meyer remembers thinking when he first heard the US president say it. His response to Trump's claim is blunt. The notion of a mass attack on the white Afrikaner minority in South Africa does not exist, he told the BBC, adding that his identity gave him the legitimacy to say so. Meyer was one of the chief mediators to end white-minority rule, known as apartheid, in South Africa in the 1990s.

stories.title: La Belgique renoue avec le Rwanda et conserve son influence en Afrique centrale
stories.summary: Publicité La Belgique renoue avec le Rwanda et conserve son influence en Afrique centrale Afrique La Belgique et le Rwanda ont annoncé, en marge de l'Assemblée générale des Nations Unies à New-York, le rétablissement de leurs relations diplomatiques. Ces dernières avaient été rompues il y a un an et demi après des sanctions de l'Union européenne contre des chefs militaires rwandais, dans le cadre du conflit entre la République démocratique du Congo et l'AFC/M23 soutenu par le Rwanda. Publié le : 25/09/2026 - 16:33 Modifié le : 25/09/2026 - 16:36 4 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Le chef de la diplomatie belge, Maxime Prévot, aux côtés de son homologue rwandais, Olivier Nduhungirehe, à New York, sur une photo postée le 23 septembre 2026 sur Facebook. © Ministère des Affaires étrangères et de la coopération internationale rwandais/FACEBOOK Après un an et demi de rupture, la Belgique et le Rwanda ont renoué leurs relations diplomatiques cette semaine du 21 septembre, en marge de l'Assemblée générale de l'ONU à New York. stories.summary: Publicité Législatives au Maroc, "Deportation Project" de Trump, nouveau conflit en Éthiopie : l'hebdo Afrique Récap Afrique Publié le : 25/09/2026 - 11:23 Modifié le : 25/09/2026 - 12:22 6 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Un électeur vote le 23 septembre 2026, lors des élections législatives marocaines, dans un bureau de vote installé dans une école du quartier Youssoufia à Rabat. © Abdel Majid Bziouat, AFP • En Éthiopie, un nouveau conflit semble prendre forme. Africa’s young demographic – it is the world’s youngest continent with 70% of people aged under 30 – is seen as its greatest asset . But a lack of cohesion between education institutions and employers means graduates in Africa, whose number is rising, are not well prepared when they start work, Nkengasong says.

stories.summary: AGOA Reauthorized Through 2028 - A Critical Victory and a Call to Action for Continental Engagement AGOA CSO Network The AGOA CSO Network is urging civil society, private-sector leaders, and government stakeholders to prioritize AGOA modernization in national and regional consultations to strengthen its long-term prospects. 23 September 2026 Content from a Premium Partner AGOA Civil Society Network (Washington, DC) Washington, DC — The AGOA Civil Society Organization (CSO) Network welcomes the U.S. Congress’s decision to extend the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) through December 31, 2028. This extension ensures continued duty-free access for thousands of African products and strengthens one of the continent’s most important trade frameworks. Africa’s exports under AGOA exceeded US$30 billion in 2024, with key growth in apparel, agriculture, minerals, and automotive components. While this renewal is a significant achievement, it requires immediate and coordinated efforts to modernize AGOA and secure its long-term future.

stories.title: How Ceuta, football and Israel are shaping Morocco's election
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Moroccan voters will find candidates from 27 parties on the ballot By Basma El Atti Published 22 September 2026 Disillusioned young voters in Morocco were courted with viral football slogans, promises of one million jobs and anti-Israel rallying calls ahead of Wednesday's parliamentary elections. Yet, for many young Moroccans, politics remains deeply disconnected from reality. "I have no hope for this election. I'm ashamed of our political scene. It's a complete circus," Siham Azeroual, 32, an environmental activist who lives in the Atlas region, tells the BBC. The outcome of the vote will decide the make-up of the next government, just weeks after 60,000 people risked their lives to cross from the North African country to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta - a sign of the lack of opportunities many young people feel they have at home.

stories.title: 'I have never felt heat like that' - a survivor on watching 33 cellmates die in Nigeria
stories.summary: Image caption, Usman Muhammad survived but 33 others died in the cell and four others died later in hospital By Madina Maishanu BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Minna Published 22 September 2026 Usman Muhammad pauses by the entrance to a tiny Nigerian prison cell and leans his forehead against the wall unable to speak. The day before he had been trapped inside the stifling room, measuring roughly 6m (19.7ft) by 3m (9.8ft), with more than 50 other prisoners. Thirty-three of his cellmates died in the cramped conditions in the prison in Minna, the capital of Nigeria's Niger state - and four died later in hospital. The mass deaths caused an outcry and sparked protests , including attacks on public buildings, as relatives and locals demanded answers. Federal officials had initially blamed the deaths on a diphtheria outbreak but exactly what happened is now the subject of an investigation. "I have never felt heat like that in my life.

stories.title: Using AI to ‘talk to animals’ might make us feel clever – but what, if anything, does it do for them?
stories.summary: Vivek Thakker/The Guardian Using AI to ‘talk to animals’ might make us feel clever – but what, if anything, does it do for them? As animal behaviorists increasingly use AI in their research, they grapple with how to wield the technology responsibly I’m sitting in a small boat in Shark Bay, Australia, eavesdropping on a conversation between some of Earth’s most intelligent beings. The motor is off, the turquoise sea is glassy, and Stephanie King and I are motionless, transfixed by the whistles, clicks and squeezy, whirring noises made by the dolphins swimming below us. If anyone could tell me what these big-brained social mammals are saying, it would be her. Based at the University of Bristol, she co-leads Shark Bay Dolphin Research , one of the longest-running wild dolphin research projects in the world.
